beats.caption: An EPC contractor engineers, buys and builds the whole job
beats.text: EPC stands for engineering, procurement and construction. One firm signs a contract to design the plant, order the equipment and run the crews that install it, usually for a fixed price or a guaranteed finish date. The owner gets one party to hold accountable instead of juggling dozens of trades.

beats.caption: Engineering comes first: the layout is drawn before steel goes up
beats.text: Engineers size the substation, switchgear, generators, chillers and piping, then lay every room, duct and cable tray out on drawings. On a data center the design is driven by the IT load in megawatts and the rack density, which sets how much power and cooling each hall needs.

beats.caption: Procurement: long-lead gear is ordered years ahead
beats.text: Large power transformers now take two to four years to arrive, and big switchgear and chillers well over a year. The EPC firm places those orders early, often before the design is final, and tracks every crate to the laydown yard. Whoever has secured factory slots can promise earlier dates.

beats.caption: Construction: crews set the gear and tie power and water in
beats.text: Cranes lift transformers and chillers onto pads, electricians pull cable and land it in switchgear, pipefitters join the chilled-water loops, and the hall is commissioned system by system. A large AI campus can have thousands of workers on site, and electrical and mechanical work is most of the cost.

beats.caption: One late part slips the date the capacity comes online
beats.text: If a transformer arrives late, everything it feeds waits: racks sit dark and the owner's revenue start slides. On a fixed-price job the contractor eats overruns, so margins depend on execution. Backlog at these firms has surged with AI builds. Related: Quanta Services (PWR), EMCOR (EME), Comfort Systems USA (FIX), Sterling Infrastructure (STRL).
